source.note: Scan without a text layer. The PDF includes the cover (printed page 1), the instructions (page 2) and the information sheet (page 14); PDF page n = printed page n. The instructions mention a special answer book, which is not in this PDF. Source file and hash are recorded in sources/maths/manifest.json. Duration 3 hours as printed on the cover.

extraction.method: manual transcription from 170 dpi page renders, checked at 400 dpi where needed

questions.stem_md:
The matric class of a certain high school had to vote for the chairperson of the RCL (representative council of learners). The scatter plot below shows the IQ (intelligence quotient) of the 10 learners who received the most votes and the number of votes that they received.

Before the election, the popularity of each of these ten learners was established and a popularity score (out of a 100) was assigned to each. The popularity scores and the number of votes of the same 10 learners who received the most votes are shown in the table below.

table.caption: Popularity scores and the number of votes of the same 10 learners who received the most votes.

questions.stem_md: Calculate the:

questions.text_md: Mean number of votes that these 10 learners received
Standard deviation of the number of votes that these 10 learners received
The learners who received fewer votes than one standard deviation below the mean were not invited for an interview. How many learners were invited?
Determine the equation of the least squares regression line for the data given in the table.
Predict the number of votes that a learner with a popularity score of 72 will receive.

questions.stem_md: Using the scatter plot and table above, provide a reason why:

questions.text_md: IQ is not a good indicator of the number of votes that a learner could receive
The prediction in QUESTION 1.4 is reliable

questions.stem_md: A company conducted research among all its employees on what percentage of their monthly salary was spent on fuel in a particular month. The data is represented in the ogive (cumulative frequency graph) below.

questions.text_md: How many people are employed at this company?
Write down the modal class of the data.
How many employees spent more than 22,5% of their monthly salary on fuel?
An employee spent R2 400 of his salary on fuel in that particular month. Determine the monthly salary of this employee if he spends 7% of his salary on fuel.
questions.notes: No dedicated skill for a percentage-of-salary calculation (R2 400 is 7% of the salary); tagged with stat.ogive as the question-context skill.

questions.text_md: The monthly salaries of these employees remains constant and the number of litres of fuel used in each month also remains constant. If the fuel price increases from R21,43 per litre to R22,79 per litre at the beginning of the next month, how will the above ogive change?

questions.text_md: Calculate the coordinates of P.

From point A, another tangent is drawn to touch the circle with centre M at B.

questions.text_md: Show that the length of tangent AB is given by $\sqrt{2t^{2}+4t+9}$.
questions.notes: No dedicated skill for the length of a tangent from an external point; tagged with ageo.distance-formula and ageo.circle-equation.

questions.text_md: Determine the minimum length of AB.

questions.stem_md:
Given that $\sqrt{13}\sin x+3=0$, where $x\in(90^{\circ}\,;\,270^{\circ})$.

Without using a calculator, determine the value of:

questions.text_md: $\tan x$

Determine the value of the following expression, without using a calculator:

$\dfrac{\cos(90^{\circ}+\theta)}{\sin(\theta-180^{\circ})+3\sin(-\theta)}$

Determine the general solution of the following equation:

$(\cos x+2\sin x)(3\sin 2x-1)=0$

questions.stem_md: Given the identity: $\cos(x+y)\cdot\cos(x-y)=1-\sin^{2}x-\sin^{2}y$

questions.text_md: Prove the identity.
Hence, determine the value of $1-\sin^{2}45^{\circ}-\sin^{2}15^{\circ}$, without using a calculator.

questions.stem_md: Consider the trigonometric expression: $16\sin x\cdot\cos^{3}x-8\sin x\cdot\cos x$

questions.text_md: Rewrite the expression as a single trigonometric ratio.
For which value of $x$ in the interval $x\in[0^{\circ}\,;\,90^{\circ}]$ will $16\sin x\cdot\cos^{3}x-8\sin x\cdot\cos x$ have its minimum value?

questions.stem_md: In the diagram below, the graphs of $f(x)=\tan x$ and $g(x)=2\sin 2x$ are drawn for the interval $x\in[-180^{\circ}\,;\,180^{\circ}]$. $\mathrm{A}(60^{\circ}\,;\,k)$ and B are two points of intersection of $f$ and $g$.

questions.text_md: Write down the period of $g$.

questions.stem_md: Calculate the:

questions.text_md: Value of $k$
Coordinates of B
Write down the range of $2g(x)$.
For which values of $x$ will $g(x+5^{\circ})-f(x+5^{\circ})\leq 0$ in the interval $x\in[-90^{\circ}\,;\,0^{\circ}]$?
Determine the values of $p$ for which $\sin x\cdot\cos x=p$ will have exactly two real roots in the interval $x\in[-180^{\circ}\,;\,180^{\circ}]$.

questions.stem_md:
AB is a vertical flagpole that is $\sqrt{5}\,p$ metres long. AC and AD are two cables anchoring the flagpole. B, C and D are in the same horizontal plane.

BD $=2p$ metres, $A\hat{C}D=x$ and $A\hat{D}C=45^{\circ}$.

questions.text_md: Determine the length of AD in terms of $p$.
Show that the length of CD $=\dfrac{3p(\sin x+\cos x)}{\sqrt{2}\sin x}$.
If it is further given that $p=10$ and $x=110^{\circ}$, calculate the area of $\Delta$ADC.

questions.stem_md:
In the diagram, O is the centre of the circle. MNPR is a cyclic quadrilateral and SN is a diameter of the circle. Chord MS and radius OR are drawn. $\hat{M}_{2}=64^{\circ}$.

Determine, giving reasons, the size of the following angles:

questions.text_md: $\hat{P}$

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, $\Delta$ABG is drawn. D and E are midpoints of AB and AG respectively. AG and BG are produced to C and H respectively. F is a point on BC such that FG $\parallel$ CH.

questions.text_md: Give a reason why DE $\parallel$ BH.
If it is further given that $\dfrac{\mathrm{FC}}{\mathrm{BF}}=\dfrac{1}{4}$, DE $=3x-1$ and GH $=x+1$, calculate, giving reasons, the value of $x$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, O is the centre of a circle. OD bisects chord AB.
questions.text_md: Prove the theorem that states that the line from the centre of a circle that bisects a chord is perpendicular to the chord, i.e. OD $\perp$ AB.
